rows.basis: Growth in gross 'Servers and networking equipment': 172,492m − 113,156m = 59,336m, against cash purchases of PP&E of 131,819m. The figure counts all server and network growth, not only AI, and is net of disposals. It excludes construction in progress (+25.1bn, the mixed shell), land and buildings, finance leases and purchase commitments of 84.8bn, which the note does not split by AI. The release says the rise in net purchases 'primarily reflects investments in artificial intelligence', but gives no amount.

Growth in gross 'Equipment': 218,893m − 185,039m = 33,854m, against capex of 82,999m. The server category was not reported separately before the FY2025 10-K, so this wider category includes heavy equipment and other equipment used in fulfillment. The FY2024 Equipment value is unresolved against XBRL.

Growth in gross 'Equipment': 185,039m − 157,458m = 27,581m, against capex of 52,729m. This includes heavy (fulfillment) and other equipment as well as servers. It predates most of the generative-AI buildout and is mostly general compute and logistics, so it is an upper bound on any AI part.

Growth in gross 'Equipment': 157,458m − 128,683m = 28,775m, against capex of 63,645m. This includes heavy (fulfillment) and other equipment as well as servers. It predates the generative-AI buildout and is mostly general compute and logistics, so it is an upper bound on any AI part.

Guidance is for total capex, not the AI part. The February 5 2026 release said about $200bn 'across Amazon in 2026', citing AI, chips, robotics and satellites. The Q2 2026 release raised this to approximately $220bn. Quarterly releases say the increase 'primarily reflects investments in artificial intelligence', but no AI amount or share is stated.

The FY2025 MD&A expects technology and infrastructure spending to increase 'including to support our artificial intelligence and machine learning initiatives'. This is words only, with no amount or share.

The Q3 2025 release gives Amazon Connect, one AI contact-center product, a $1bn annualized revenue run rate 'in recent weeks'. That is a single product's run rate, not fiscal-year AI revenue. AWS (128,725m) is a cloud segment, not the AI line, and is not counted.

The Q2 2026 release says AWS's AI business 'exceeded a $25 billion annual revenue run rate', growing triple digits. This is a run rate at mid-2026, not revenue recognized in the fiscal year, which has not yet closed. No revenue total is in the pack, so no share is computed.
